content: CHATGPT CONNECTOR 404/401 AUDIT — VERIFIED DIAGNOSIS 2026-05-20. Symptom: ChatGPT receiving 404/401 calling the stack; tool namespace visible but invocation fails. Verified via header instrumentation (commit d6c9721), NOT inferred. ROOT CAUSE: OpenAI evolved its MCP connector to openai-mcp/1.0.0 which (a) attempts Streamable HTTP transport (POST /openai/sse, Accept: application/json+text/event-stream) and (b) sends NO authorization header at all — it expects OAuth/CIMD discovery, not the static bearer the openai bridge requires. The bridge's 401 is a dead-end JSON with no WWW-Authenticate pointer, so ChatGPT can't discover where to get a token, sends none, gets 401. EVIDENCE OUR CODE IS CLEAN: openai bridge (clients/openai_bridge/, sse_server.py openai routes) UNCHANGED since v1.4.0 commit fade269 (May 9); the entire scribe arc never touched it; new ask_scribe tool safely Ring-3-excluded (is_ring_3=True, never exposed), manifest builds fine. So v1.5.0 did NOT break it — the regression is client-side (OpenAI connector update, confirmed by ChatGPT-seat research: Help Center updated, connectors renamed to apps, OAuth/CIMD/DCR emphasized; SSE still supported so transport is NOT the blocker, AUTH is). FIX SCOPE (focused session, security-sensitive auth membrane): port grok_bridge/oauth.py (OAuth 2.1 auth_code + PKCE + RFC 8414/9728 metadata + WWW-Authenticate 401 pointer + identity_gate validator) to openai_bridge, PLUS add the piece Grok lacks — a Dynamic Client Registration endpoint (RFC 7591), since ChatGPT's connector expects to self-register. Wire .well-known/* + oauth/* routes into sse_server.py openai middleware; add tunnel ingress rules for /openai/oauth/* and /openai/.well-known/*. Test against ChatGPT with header diagnostics live; iterate. OPEN UNKNOWN: whether ChatGPT completes with auth_code+PKCE+DCR or needs CIMD specifically — resolve by instrumented iteration. Stack otherwise healthy: bridge+SSE up at v1.5.0, 79 tools, scribe breathing.
